title: Psychophysics of Duration Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.33176v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Studies of time perception in language models focus mainly on text-based settings. Yet multimodal models are increasingly used for tasks that require perceiving the passage of time, making the limits of their temporal perception important to understand. We measure the limits of duration perception from audio against a human baseline to address this gap. Drawing from psychophysics, we operationalise duration perception as a melody recognition task, testing when a melody becomes unrecognisable as it is slowed down. Of 21 tested models, most cannot recognise well-known melodies without labelled in-context examples. With in-context examples, seven recognise melodies reliably, most peaking within the median human recognition band. translated_title: 多模态大语言模型时长感知的心理物理学研究
translated_abstract: 针对语言模型时间感知的研究主要集中在基于文本的环境中。然而，多模态模型正越来越多地被应用于需要感知时间流逝的任务，因此理解其时间感知的极限变得十分重要。为了填补这一空白，我们以人类表现为基线，测量了模型从音频中感知时长的极限。借鉴心理物理学的方法，我们将时长感知操作化为一个旋律识别任务，测试旋律在被放慢到什么程度时会变得无法识别。在测试的21个模型中，大多数模型在没有标注上下文示例的情况下无法识别知名旋律。在提供上下文示例后，有七个模型能够可靠地识别旋律，其中大多数模型的识别峰值落在人类识别能力的中位数区间内。模型的泛化能力有限：(i) 识别峰值会随上下文示例的速度发生偏移，(ii) 旋律标题会引发预测偏差，(iii) 提供带有科学音高记谱法的示例并不能阻止准确率下降。
tldr: 该论文首次借鉴心理物理学方法，将旋律减速识别作为时长感知的量化任务，系统测量了多模态大语言模型的听觉时长感知极限，发现仅七个模型能在上下文示例辅助下可靠识别被放慢的旋律且多数峰值接近人类中位水平，但其泛化能力仍存在明显局限。
en_tdlr: Drawing on psychophysics, this study operationalizes duration perception as a melody-slowing recognition task to systematically measure the temporal perception limits of multimodal LLMs, finding that only seven of 21 tested models reliably recognize slowed melodies—with most peaks within the median human recognition band—while their generalization remains limited.
